pillars.name: Regulatory Functions
pillars.description: The substantive regulatory functions a supervisory authority performs, regardless of sector — governance, policy-making, authorisation, supervision, enforcement, financial crime, crisis management, capability building. Financial Supervisors audience only.

pillars.name: Business Functions
pillars.description: The core internal departments of a regulated firm — compliance, risk management, legal, treasury, governance, client money, product governance, trading, third-party oversight, actuarial. Firms audience only.

pillars.name: Cross-Cutting Themes
pillars.description: Risks and disciplines that run through every pillar and every sector rather than belonging to one — e.g. operational resilience, sustainable finance, consumer protection, cross-border supervision, data & technology infrastructure.

pillars.name: Generic Supervisory Skills
pillars.description: Skills that let regulatory staff function effectively across every pillar and sector — management, communication, judgement, and technology skills not tied to a particular financial sector.

pillars.name: Sector Programmes
pillars.description: Technical, subject-matter training for supervising particular parts of the financial sector (banking, insurance, investment funds, payments, pensions, etc.) and specialist cross-sector technical themes (digital assets, AI, sustainable finance, cybersecurity, SupTech).

courses.title: Market Abuse Detection & Surveillance
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how market abuse is detected through surveillance systems, and how supervisors assess the adequacy of firms' own surveillance and monitoring capability.

courses.title: Market Infrastructure Supervision: CCPs, CSDs and Trading Venues
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of the regulatory framework for central counterparties, central securities depositories, and trading venues, and the supervisory considerations specific to critical market infrastructure.

courses.title: Mastering Investment Services Regulations (EU Edition)
courses.summary: Understanding regulations impacting investment services.

courses.title: Mastering Time Management & Prioritisation
courses.summary: Learn practical tools for managing competing demands and focusing on high-value activities.

courses.title: Measuring Supervisory Effectiveness
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in designing and using metrics that meaningfully measure supervisory effectiveness and outcomes, drawing on approaches used in international assessments such as IMF/World Bank Financial Sector Assessment Programs (FSAPs).

courses.title: Mentoring Conversations That Work
courses.summary: Learn how to hold effective coaching conversations that support colleagues’ development and motivation.

courses.title: MiCA and Beyond: Exploring Crypto-Assets Regulation (EU Edition)
courses.summary: Introduced the purpose and drivers of the MiCA Regulation, the roles of different operators in the crypto-asset ecosystem, the implications of PSD2 for crypto-asset service providers, and the operational and custody considerations supervisors should apply to EMT/ART issuers and…

courses.title: MiCA & Supervising CASPs (EU Edition)
courses.summary: Learn how to apply MiCA requirements when assessing and supervising crypto-asset service providers.

courses.title: Money Market Funds: Regulation and Systemic Risk
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how money market funds are regulated under money market fund rules and the systemic risk considerations that drive regulatory reform, and the supervisory tools used to assess MMF resilience.

courses.title: Navigating Capital Market Regulations (EU Edition)
courses.summary: Gaining insights into the capital market regulatory environment.

courses.title: Negotiation, Persuasion & Critical Thinking
courses.summary: Learn how to use structured reasoning and communication strategies to negotiate effectively and make well-reasoned decisions.

courses.title: Open Banking and Third-Party Provider Access
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how open banking access rights operate under payment services legislation, and the supervisory considerations for account information and payment initiation service providers.

courses.title: Operational Resilience Testing and Scenario Analysis
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how firms design and test operational resilience scenarios, and how supervisors assess the adequacy of impact tolerances and testing programmes.

courses.title: Outcomes-Based Compliance Supervision
courses.summary: Introduce the outcomes-based compliance supervision methodology and its role in effective, efficient supervision.

courses.title: Passporting and Cross-Border Authorisation
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how passporting and cross-border authorisation regimes operate in practice, and the cooperation expected between home and host supervisors.

courses.title: Payment Fraud and APP Scam Prevention
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how payment fraud, including authorised push payment scams, is regulated and prevented, and the supervisory considerations around liability allocation and fraud reporting.

courses.title: Performance Measurement and Disclosure Supervision
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how investment performance is measured, attributed, and disclosed, and how supervisors assess the accuracy and fairness of performance claims used in marketing.

courses.title: Private Markets & Alternative Asset Supervision
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how private equity, private credit and real asset funds are structured and supervised, including the supervisory implications of the retailisation of private markets under retail-oriented long-term fund regimes.

courses.title: Procedural Fairness in Enforcement Decisions
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of the principles of procedural fairness that must be applied in enforcement decision-making, including the right to make representations and managing conflicts of interest.

courses.title: PSD3/PSR: Transition and Supervisory Implications (EU Edition)
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of the key changes introduced by PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation compared to PSD2, and the practical implications for supervisors managing the transition.

courses.title: Public Speaking and Presentation Skills: From Preparation to Delivery
courses.summary: Learn how to design and deliver presentations with clarity, confidence, and impact.

courses.title: Recovery and Resolution Planning for Supervisors
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in assessing the credibility of firms' recovery plans and understanding the supervisor's role in resolution planning and resolvability assessment.

courses.title: Regulatory Impact Assessment in Practice
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build practical skills in assessing the impact of proposed rules — costs and benefits to industry and consumers, proportionality, and identifying unintended consequences before rules are finalised.

courses.title: Report Writing for Regulatory Impact
courses.summary: Learn how to produce clear, structured, and compelling regulatory reports that support effective supervisory decisions.

courses.title: Risk-Based Supervision of Payment Institutions
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in applying a risk-based approach to supervising payment institutions, drawing on published supervisory guidance in this area, including how to assess safeguarding of client funds.

courses.title: Risk-Based Supervision: Prioritisation Under Resource Constraints
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in designing and applying a risk-based supervisory approach that allocates limited supervisory resource to the areas of greatest risk, addressing the common challenge of unclear mandates and resource constraints.

courses.title: Risk Governance & Thematic Review Panels
courses.summary: Prepares supervisory staff to participate effectively in risk governance panels (RGPs) and thematic review panels (TRPs) — internal governance mechanisms used to review and challenge supervisory assessments and thematic findings.

courses.title: Running an Effective Regulatory Consultation
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in designing and running an effective public consultation on proposed rules, including stakeholder engagement strategy and how to analyse and respond to consultation feedback transparently.

courses.title: Sanctions Compliance Supervision
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in supervising firms' sanctions compliance frameworks, including screening obligations and assessment of control effectiveness.

courses.title: Securing and Defending Operational Independence
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of the practical and legal foundations of supervisory independence, and how authorities defend and account for that independence to government and other stakeholders.

courses.title: Senior Leadership Workshops
courses.summary: Deliver focused workshop content targeting senior leadership capability.

courses.title: Setting Regulatory Strategy and Priorities
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to equip participants with the skills to translate a supervisory authority's statutory mandate into a strategic plan and prioritised work programme, balancing risk, resource, and stakeholder expectations.

courses.title: Setting Supervisory Tolerance and Strategy for Cyber Risk
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in establishing a supervisory tolerance for cyber-related harm and prioritising supervisory resource allocation across the regulated population.

courses.title: Settlement and Negotiated Outcomes in Enforcement
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of the practical and strategic considerations in negotiating settlements with firms under investigation, including when settlement is and is not appropriate.

courses.title: Spotting AI System Vulnerabilities
courses.summary: Learn from real-world case studies how regulators use AI to strengthen oversight and efficiency.

courses.title: Stablecoins, E-Money Tokens & Asset-Referenced Tokens (EU Edition)
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how stablecoin issuers structure reserves and redemption mechanisms under MiCA, and how supervisors assess run risk, reserve adequacy, and the operational resilience of EMT/ART issuers.

courses.title: Supervising AI-Driven Financial Crime Systems
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in assessing the governance, validation, and explainability of AI systems deployed by firms for AML/CFT purposes, applying supervisory judgement to model risk and human oversight controls.

courses.title: Supervising AML/CFT Obligations in Practice
courses.summary: Learn how to apply AML/CFT requirements consistently across supervisory processes and decision-making.

courses.title: Supervising Complaints Handling
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' ability to supervise firms' complaints-handling frameworks effectively, including assessing root-cause analysis practices and the operation of redress schemes, so that complaints data is used as a genuine early-warning…

courses.title: Supervising Investment Advice and Suitability
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in supervising the quality of investment advice given to clients, including suitability assessment and product governance controls.

courses.title: Supervisory Judgment
courses.summary: Strengthen participants’ skills in applying supervisory judgment across authorisation and ongoing supervision.

courses.title: Supervisory Technology Trends and Innovations
courses.summary: Understanding technological advancements in financial supervision.

courses.title: Sustainable Finance: Supervisory Insights (EU Edition)
courses.summary: Discussed sustainability risk assessments and their implications for supervised entities, equipping participants to address sustainability risk and integrate sustainable finance into day-to-day supervision.

courses.title: The Cyber Threat Landscape for Supervised Firms
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of the cyber threat landscape facing regulated firms, including internal and external threat actors and their likely targets within financial market infrastructure.

courses.title: The EU AI Act and Financial Regulation: Interplay and Overlaps (EU Edition)
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how the EU AI Act's requirements interact with existing sectoral financial regulation, including where AI Act high-risk classifications apply to financial services AI systems.

courses.title: Third-Party and Cloud Outsourcing Risk
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in assessing firms' reliance on critical third-party and cloud providers, including concentration risk and the adequacy of exit strategies.

courses.title: Tokenisation of Traditional Assets
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how traditional financial assets are tokenised and traded on distributed ledger infrastructure, and the supervisory considerations as tokenised and traditional market infrastructure converge.

courses.title: Tokenization & Digital Assets
courses.summary: Learn how tokenised products and digital assets are structured and issued under emerging regulatory frameworks.

courses.title: Understanding Business Models
courses.summary: Learn how to assess firms’ business models and link them to prudential, conduct, and AML/CFT risks.

courses.title: Understanding FinTech Models
courses.summary: Learn how different FinTech business models operate, assessing regulatory boundaries and operational risks.

courses.title: Understanding ML/TF Typologies
courses.summary: Learn how to identify key money laundering/terrorist financing typologies and recognise red flags in real-world scenarios.

courses.title: Understanding Portfolio Management Practice
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' understanding of how portfolio managers construct and manage portfolios against mandates, and how supervisors assess mandate compliance and risk budgeting practice.

courses.title: Using AI Tools at Work
courses.summary: Learn how to integrate AI productivity tools into daily workflows safely and effectively.

courses.title: Using Testing and Audit Data in Cyber Supervision
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in using a firm's own testing metrics and internal audit findings as core supervisory data sources for assessing cyber resilience.

courses.title: Workforce Planning for Specialist Regulatory Functions
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in planning and resourcing a supervisory workforce with the right mix of generalist and specialist skills, addressing recruitment and retention challenges specific to regulatory bodies.

courses.title: Writing for Impact: Supervisory Correspondence and Public Statements
courses.summary: The aim of this workshop is to build participants' skills in writing clear, authoritative supervisory correspondence and public statements that are accurate, defensible, and appropriately calibrated for their audience, from firm-level letters to public communications.
